hooks.text: A microscopic water bear can survive a high-speed crash into the Moon.
How did a tiny water bear survive a crash onto the Moon?
In 2019, thousands of living water bears crashed onto the Moon.

title: The Moon's Toughest Hitchhikers
description: Discover how tiny water bears named in 1773 survived extreme temperatures, the vacuum of space, and a lunar crash.

beats.text: A microscopic water bear can survive a high-speed crash into the Moon.
beats.visual: Beresheet lunar lander spacecraft mock-up in cleanroom, 2018

beats.text: First officially described back in 1773 by zoologist Johann [Goeze](/ɡˈOzˈi/), these tiny creatures were named little water bears.
beats.visual: Johann August Ephraim Goeze portrait painting

beats.text: They possess eight legs and typically measure less than a single millimeter in length.
beats.visual: Hypsibius exemplaris scanning electron microscope image, showing eight legs

beats.text: When environmental conditions turn harsh, they roll into a tight ball called a [tun](/tˈun/) and completely dry out.
beats.visual: Tardigrade tun state scanning electron microscope image

beats.text: Inside this glass-like slumber, they can survive temperatures near absolute zero and up to one hundred fifty degrees Celsius.
beats.visual: Ramazzottius varieornatus scanning electron microscope image in laboratory

beats.text: They are remarkably the only known animals to successfully endure the harsh vacuum of outer space.
beats.visual: Earth horizon from space viewed from the International Space Station

beats.text: That is exactly how a microscopic water bear survived a high-speed crash into the Moon.
beats.visual: Beresheet lander concept illustration over the Moon
